claim: WHO's 9 Dec 2021 technical document stated that public health spending in Ukraine had been low relative to neighboring Central European countries and that COVID-19 exposed weaknesses and under-resourcing in the health system.
limitations: The report is a financing/system-capacity assessment, not a direct measure of population health stress or conflict propensity.

claim: WHO/European Observatory reported on 23 Nov 2021 that 51% of health spending in Ukraine in 2018 was private, almost entirely out-of-pocket, leaving vulnerable groups exposed to catastrophic or impoverishing payments.
limitations: Uses 2018 spending structure to characterize a pre-2022 system condition; it does not prove worsening in late 2021.

claim: WHO's May 2021 country report described an incomplete health/decentralization reform under pandemic pressure, with mixed central/local responsibilities for public health and service delivery.
limitations: Institutional complexity can create friction but does not by itself imply system failure.

claim: WHO reported in Feb 2021 that infection-prevention-and-control improvements were achieved during the acute COVID response and that support to national and facility programs was continuing.
limitations: Improvement in IPC capability is a bounded stabilizer and does not imply full health-system resilience.

claim: OHCHR published a report on 23 Sep 2021 covering the human-rights situation in Ukraine from 1 Feb to 31 Jul 2021, providing a contemporaneous institutional sensor for conflict-affected rights and social conditions.
limitations: This row establishes an admissible source family and observation channel; subclaims on language, religion or group-specific conditions must be extracted from the report before scoring.

claim: WHO's 2023 policy brief summarizes surveys conducted in April and November 2021 showing disruptions but general continuity of primary health services. Because publication occurred in 2023, the findings are retrospective-only unless contemporaneous releases can be recovered.
limitations: Data collection occurred in 2021, but collection time is not public-observability time.
